batches.title: Real project persistence and recovery integration
batches.objective: Implement the project persistence/recovery objective that batch-97 did not complete. Inspect the current App state lifecycle and existing storage/media contracts first. Build a real user-facing persistence path that saves and restores the editable project metadata needed to resume: stable media references and asset metadata, creative brief/director intent, current director/edit plan, production blueprint, music choice/metadata, render/export settings, schema/version and recent editor state. Do not persist File objects or large media blobs in synchronous storage. On reload, restore usable metadata into the real App state and clearly distinguish restorable project metadata from media that must be re-selected or revalidated. Add deterministic schema migration, atomic/last-known-good recovery, corruption/partial-write handling and truthful missing-media state. Integrate save/load into the actual App lifecycle, not merely a utility. Add focused production verification that exercises save/load, reload-after-edit, migration, corruption, partial state and missing media; run build and existing relevant verification. Preserve Blob/Gemini/music/renderer contracts and do not modify .github/workflows/**, builder/runner/**, builder/quality/**, config/autonomous-builder-queue.json, scripts/prepare-autonomous-batch.mjs, Vercel infrastructure, secrets or the protected renderer. No automatic merge or deployment. The result must be substantive production behaviour and must prove the user can continue editing after recovery.

batches.title: Social export and delivery reliability
batches.objective: Improve the production export/delivery layer for finished creator videos. Support reliable 9:16, 1:1 and 16:9 output profiles, deterministic filenames/metadata, audio/video duration agreement, export validation, progress/error states and graceful recovery from failed or unsupported export paths. Preserve browser/FFmpeg rendering and existing successful MP4 output. Restrict work to export/delivery paths and existing verification boundaries; do not modify .github/workflows/** or autonomous-runner infrastructure, AI Director/timeline logic or durable queue. Make substantive production changes and verify actual output contracts. No automatic merge or deployment.

batches.title: Mobile PWA delivery hardening
batches.objective: Harden Android/PWA delivery without redesigning the editor. Improve manifest correctness, installability, icons, viewport/mobile-safe behaviour, offline app-shell resilience and safe cache/version handling. Ensure the deployed app remains usable on Android browsers and can be installed to the home screen reliably. Restrict changes to PWA/static delivery and mobile-safe styling utilities; preserve AI Director, timeline, renderer and protected infrastructure. Prove build and installability-related contracts with substantive production behaviour. No automatic merge or deployment.

batches.title: Provider failure and recovery resilience
batches.objective: Make the product resilient when Gemini, remote APIs, media decoding or optional providers fail, time out or return malformed data. Strengthen shared request/error/recovery handling and truthful fallbacks so users receive actionable state instead of hangs, silent failures or fabricated results. Preserve local-first operation and successful paths. Restrict changes to shared request/error/recovery infrastructure and consumers; do not modify AI Director/timeline implementation, renderer, protected AutoBot infrastructure or durable queue. Make substantive production changes and verify timeout, malformed-response, offline and provider-unavailable scenarios. No automatic merge or deployment.

batches.title: Cinematic editor and renderer quality
batches.objective: Raise the existing cinematic editor/rendering quality without replacing the protected renderer. Inspect current director, timeline, render-plan and browser renderer contracts first. Implement real improvements for intelligent reframing, smooth shot-specific zoom/pan, speed changes or ramps, purposeful transition variety, cinematic colour treatment, restrained text, continuity, social-safe framing and reliable audio integration where supported. Decisions must follow director intent and available media. Preserve successful MP4 rendering and avoid black-screen regressions. Make substantive production changes, run focused behavioural checks plus production build and relevant verification. Do not modify .github/workflows/**, builder infrastructure, durable queue or protected renderer implementation. No automatic merge or deployment.

batches.title: Deterministic director story intelligence
batches.objective: Improve the universal director's story construction after the current cinematic-quality wave. Build a deterministic story-beat layer that turns verified media into an explicit hook/build/reveal/action/emotional/hero sequence according to prompt intent, media quality and subject diversity. Integrate those beats into the existing edit planner without replacing Gemini analysis, director selection, critique or the protected renderer. Preserve single-source and small-library behaviour, never invent media, expose auditable story evidence and verify production build plus focused story contracts. Do not modify .github/workflows/**, builder infrastructure, durable queue, Vercel infrastructure, secrets or src/renderer.js. No automatic merge or deployment.

batches.title: Autonomous builder self-improvement
batches.objective: Continuously improve the quality of future AutoBot work using evidence from its own verified run history. Analyse completed units, detect repeated shallow/unchanged patterns, record bounded quality-gate proposals, improve task-design recommendations and refresh authoritative project context. The self-improvement loop must remain deterministic, reviewable and bounded: it must never silently rewrite protected runner/workflow/quality infrastructure, bypass verification, fabricate product capabilities or auto-merge/deploy. Changes to protected builder control logic require normal human review.
